title: Psalms 39
paragraphs: ¹ I said, "I will watch my ways and keep my tongue from sin; I will put a muzzle on my mouth while the wicked are in my presence." ² So I stayed utterly silent; I kept silent even from good things, but my anguish increased. ³ My heart grew hot within me; as I meditated, a fire burned. Then I spoke with my tongue: ⁴ "LORD, show me my end and what is the measure of my days; let me know how fleeting my life is. ⁵ You have made my days a mere handbreadth; the span of my years is nothing before you. Everyone is but a breath, even those who seem secure."

⁶ "Surely everyone goes about like a mere phantom; in vain they rush and fret. They heap up wealth without knowing whose it will finally be. ⁷ "But now, Lord, what do I look for? My hope is in you. ⁸ Save me from all my transgressions; do not make me the scorn of fools. ⁹ I was silent; I would not open my mouth, for you are the one who has done this. ¹⁰ Remove your scourge from me; I am overcome by the blow of your hand."

¹¹ "When you rebuke and discipline anyone for their sin, you consume their wealth like a moth — surely everyone is but a breath. ¹² Hear my prayer, LORD; listen to my cry for help; do not be deaf to my weeping. I dwell with you as a foreigner, a stranger, as all my ancestors were. ¹³ Look away from me, that I may smile again, before I depart and am no more."
